The growth was supported by favorable aluminum macros, higher premiums, and value-added products.  Consolidated EBITDA stood at INR128b (against our estimate of INR113b), up 43% YoY but down 8% QoQ due to higher coal and CP Coke costs, which were partially offset by a rise in sulfuric-acid prices.  APAT came in at INR73b against our estimate of INR65b (+50% YoY and - 16% QoQ) in 2QFY27.

Aluminum business  Upstream revenue stood at INR134b in 2QFY27 (+33% YoY) and EBITDA stood at INR70b (+55% YoY; USD2,125/t) supported by favorable aluminum macros, higher premiums, and value-added upstream products.  Downstream revenue stood at INR55b (+45% YoY), whereas downstream EBITDA stood at INR3.3b (+26% YoY), supported by favorable product mix, premiumization and higher shipments.

The outlook remains dependent on Middle East supply normalization and incremental capacity of ~1.5mt from Indonesia.  Industry consensus indicates LME aluminum prices of USD2,600-2,800/t for next year, although geopolitical developments could materially alter the supply- demand balance.  Management is evaluating new upstream capex over LME assumption of ~USD2,600/t, targeting project IRRs in mid-teens.
